items.title: China's broadcast and online audio-visual market reaches dual 1bn-user scale

extra.hover: 【China's broadcast and online audio-visual market reaches dual 1bn-user scale】A government report released Nov. 3 in Beijing said that by end-2025 China’s TV big-screen users exceeded 1.0 billion and online audio-visual users totaled 1.099 billion. Total TV big‑screen viewing in 2025 reached 638.7 billion hours, with average daily linear viewing of 4 hours 5 minutes; average daily online audio‑visual use was 201 minutes. The radio, TV and online audio‑visual industry generated 1.546 trillion yuan in revenue in 2025, up 5.22% YoY and up 67.82% versus the end of the 13th Five‑Year Plan; revenue from online audio‑visual service providers accounted for 53.63% of the total.

items.title: Mediolanum says bond-market stress may persist

extra.hover: 【Mediolanum says bond-market stress may persist】Mediolanum International Fund's head of fixed income said the difficult bond-market environment may persist, but current yield levels are already too high. "We expect central banks to take a less hawkish stance to ease the degree of financial tightening priced by markets, which will push down long-term yields." The firm remains constructive on government bonds given elevated yields. It added the credit outlook depends on whether policymakers act too slowly: "The longer yields stay high, the greater the pressure on credit."

items.title: CITIC Securities Ming Ming: Uneven recovery; rate cut may come in H2 next year

extra.hover: 【CITIC Securities Ming Ming: Uneven recovery; rate cut may come in H2 next year】CITIC Securities chief economist Ming Ming said global growth shows pronounced K-shaped divergence and China is experiencing an uneven, volatile recovery. He forecasts China GDP growth around 4.5% in 2027. Consumption should warm modestly, with retail sales shifting toward smart products; he sees 2027 total retail sales growth near 1%. Macro policy will be more proactive: fiscal policy is expected to expand modestly with the deficit ratio to remain about 4.0%. On monetary policy he said a rate cut may occur in H2 next year. He expects the renminbi to appreciate modestly to roughly 6.4–6.5 in 2027 and that RMB internationalization could accelerate over the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

items.title: IEA: European gas inventories at lowest since 2013, outlook worrying

extra.hover: 【IEA: European gas inventories at lowest since 2013, outlook worrying】The IEA said in its latest report EU gas storage entering the 2026-27 heating season is at its lowest level since 2013, increasing Europe’s reliance on global LNG. To replenish depleted reserves this summer Europe may need to sharply boost LNG purchases, which could extend global supply tightness into next year.

items.title: Firm: Weaker data, tighter financial conditions may reduce odds of Fed December rate hike

extra.hover: 【Firm: Weaker data, tighter financial conditions may reduce odds of Fed December rate hike】JoAnne Bianco, senior investment strategist at BondBloxx Asset Management, said weaker labor-market data, signs of slowing consumer demand or further tightening in financial conditions could lower the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. She added that slower growth and easing inf pressures would make the Fed more comfortable holding rates steady and that markets can rapidly reprice rate expectations if new data undermines the economic-resilience narrative. LSEG money-market pricing currently implies a 74% probability of a 25bp December hike.

items.title: IEA: Iran war could cause largest annual drop in global LNG supply

extra.hover: 【IEA: Iran war could cause largest annual drop in global LNG supply】The IEA warns an Iran war would disrupt supplies and intensify competition among buyers, creating severe tightness in the global gas market. It now forecasts this year’s global LNG supply will fall a record 3%, roughly 20 bcm. Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions and Iranian strikes on regional infrastructure have sharply cut Qatar and UAE exports; about 20% of LNG shipments previously transited the Strait. The IEA expects Hormuz trade flows to remain severely disrupted at least through year-end. New North American and African projects plus higher feedgas to existing plants in Africa, Asia and Russia lifted non-Gulf output 14% March–October, offsetting roughly two-thirds of Gulf losses, but the IEA still estimates global LNG output fell about 6% during the conflict.

items.title: PBOC raises foreign-currency deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4%, effective Nov 15, 2026

extra.hover: 【PBOC raises foreign-currency deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4%, effective Nov 15, 2026】China's central bank said it will raise the foreign-currency deposit reserve ratio by 2 percentage points to 6% from 4%, effective November 15, 2026. China Minsheng Bank chief economist Wen Bin said a large trade surplus and sustained corporate foreign-exchange conversion demand have been the main drivers of recent renminbi appreciation. The PBOC said the move will freeze roughly $20-25 bln of foreign-exchange liquidity at banks, help rebalance onshore FX supply and demand, curb one-sided renminbi appreciation expectations and stabilise the foreign-exchange market.

items.title: WGC sees India’s 2026 gold demand at six-year low (~650 tonnes)

extra.hover: 【WGC sees India’s 2026 gold demand at six-year low (~650 tonnes)】World Gold Council (WGC) said on Tuesday high gold prices have suppressed jewelry sales and investment, and it expects India’s 2026 gold demand to fall to about 650 tonnes, the lowest since 2020. Sachin Jain, head of WGC India, said year-to-date gold jewelry demand has declined and will drag down annual demand. India’s Q3 gold demand fell 29% YoY to 162.5 tonnes; jewelry purchases were down 20% and investment demand down 40%. Seasonal buying around Diwali and the wedding season could support a fourth-quarter rebound.

items.title: India hikes gold import duty to 15%; informal imports surge to ~50 t in Q3

extra.hover: 【India hikes gold import duty to 15%; informal imports surge to ~50 t in Q3】World Gold Council says informal gold inflows into India jumped after New Delhi more than doubled the import duty to 15%. Citing Metals Focus, the WGC reports informal imports rose to about 50 t in Q3 (Jul–Sep), up over 15x from 3 t a year earlier; the report did not detail tracking methods. The council noted higher import taxes historically increase incentives for unofficial inflows, typically via smuggling or individuals carrying small amounts. The duty rise was aimed at curbing gold demand and narrowing a trade deficit widened by higher energy prices; India remains the world’s second-largest gold consumer.
